content.content: 1	Large Language Model (LLM) evaluation results vary across reproductions, but variance sources interact, and their relative importance shifts with the benchmark format. No unified factorial framework exists to decompose these sources simultaneously across benchmarks. We apply Generalizability theory (G-theory) in a crossed design with seven facets across eight open-weight 7--9B parameter models and five benchmarks, totaling 2.3 million evaluation records. Our results suggest a format-associated variance pattern: on multiple-choice benchmarks, item-related variance---item difficulty plus model$\times$item differential item functioning (DIF)---concentrates at 68--72\%, while on free-form benchmarks it disperses to 31--41\%, with no overlap across all five benchmarks. Model$\times$item interaction (up to 36\%) is the second-largest component in cross-model analysis, consistent with prior findings on differential item functioning. Under binary scoring, BF16 and FP16 numerical precisions are functionally interchangeable ($<$0.1\% interaction). Multi-facet designs require 10$\times$ fewer items than single-condition designs to reach a generalizability coefficient of 0.80 (55 versus 552 items), and cross-model projections confirm the ratio exceeds 10$\times$ across all benchmarks, with free-form benchmarks showing nearly double the efficiency gain of multiple-choice benchmarks. Within-family scale validation (3B--9B) confirms the item-dominated variance structure is scale-invariant. We release an open-source G-theory pipeline and D-study budget calculator for evaluation design optimization.

file.content: Large Language Model (LLM) evaluation results vary across reproductions, but variance sources interact, and their relative importance shifts with the benchmark format. No unified factorial framework exists to decompose these sources simultaneously across benchmarks. We apply Generalizability theory (G-theory) in a crossed design with seven facets across eight open-weight 7--9B parameter models and five benchmarks, totaling 2.3 million evaluation records. Our results suggest a format-associated variance pattern: on multiple-choice benchmarks, item-related variance---item difficulty plus model$\times$item differential item functioning (DIF)---concentrates at 68--72\%, while on free-form benchmarks it disperses to 31--41\%, with no overlap across all five benchmarks. Model$\times$item interaction (up to 36\%) is the second-largest component in cross-model analysis, consistent with prior findings on differential item functioning. Under binary scoring, BF16 and FP16 numerical precisions are functionally interchangeable ($<$0.1\% interaction). Multi-facet designs require 10$\times$ fewer items than single-condition designs to reach a generalizability coefficient of 0.80 (55 versus 552 items), and cross-model projections confirm the ratio exceeds 10$\times$ across all benchmarks, with free-form benchmarks showing nearly double the efficiency gain of multiple-choice benchmarks. Within-family scale validation (3B--9B) confirms item dominance is scale-robust. We release an open-source G-theory pipeline and D-study budget calculator for evaluation design optimization.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Figure 3: D-Study Projection Curves — G coefficient vs. number of benchmark items."""

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patheffects as pe
import numpy as np
import os

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'serif',
    'font.serif': ['DejaVu Serif', 'Times New Roman', 'serif'],
    'font.size': 9,
    'axes.labelsize': 9,
    'xtick.labelsize': 8,
    'ytick.labelsize': 8,
    'figure.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.bbox': 'tight',
    'savefig.pad_inches': 0.08,
    'axes.spines.top': False,
    'axes.spines.right': False,
})

BLUE = '#2166ac'
RED  = '#e41a1c'
GRAY = '#666666'

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# D-study G coefficient: G(n) = n / (n + C), where C = sigma_delta / sigma_p
#
# Variance components from exp-001 single-model G-study (Henderson I, Llama-3.1-8B):
#   item_id (sigma_p): 58.4%  |  residual 23.1%  |  prompt:item 5.5%
#   seed:item 4.7%  |  precision:item 3.3%  |  temp:item 2.9%  |  ordering:item 0.8%
#
# Single-model design: 1,296 conditions/item (3 prec × 6 prompt × 6 seed × 3 temp × 4 ord)
# C = sigma_rel / sigma_p; solved from n(G≥0.80) = C / (1/0.80 - 1) = 4C
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
C_MULTI  = 13.75   # multi-facet (1,296 conditions/item); n(G≥0.80) = 55
C_SINGLE = 138.0   # single-condition (1 condition/item); n(G≥0.80) = 552

n = np.arange(1, 701)
G_m = n / (n + C_MULTI)
G_s = n / (n + C_SINGLE)

N_M80 = 55
N_S80 = 552
N_IRT = 116
G_IRT = N_IRT / (N_IRT + C_SINGLE)

stroke = [pe.withStroke(linewidth=2.5, foreground='white')]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(3.5, 2.8))

# Shaded region below G = 0.80
ax.fill_between([0, 700], 0, 0.80, color='#f4f4f4', zorder=0)

# Threshold line
ax.axhline(0.80, color=GRAY, ls='--', lw=1.0, alpha=0.7, zorder=2)

# IRT vertical line
ax.axvline(N_IRT, color='#bbbbbb', ls=':', lw=0.8, zorder=1)

# Curves
ax.plot(n, G_m, color=BLUE, lw=1.5, solid_capstyle='round', zorder=3)
ax.plot(n, G_s, color=RED, lw=1.5, ls='--', zorder=3)

# Intersection dots
for nx, c in [(N_M80, BLUE), (N_S80, RED)]:
    ax.plot(nx, 0.80, 'o', color=c, ms=4, zorder=5, mec='white', mew=0.6)

# IRT diamond
ax.plot(N_IRT, G_IRT, 'D', color='#888888', ms=3.5, zorder=5)

# --- Direct curve labels (no legend) ---
t = ax.text(320, 0.965, 'Multi-facet', fontsize=7, color=BLUE,
            ha='center', va='bottom', fontstyle='italic')
t.set_path_effects(stroke)

t = ax.text(480, 0.665, 'Single-condition', fontsize=7, color=RED,
            ha='center', va='top', fontstyle='italic')
t.set_path_effects(stroke)

# --- Annotations ---

t = ax.annotate('55 items', xy=(55, 0.80), xytext=(170, 0.63),
                fontsize=7, color=BLUE, fontweight='bold',
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=BLUE, lw=0.8),
                ha='left', zorder=6)
t.set_path_effects(stroke)

t = ax.annotate('552 items', xy=(552, 0.80), xytext=(430, 0.92),
                fontsize=7, color=RED, fontweight='bold',
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=RED, lw=0.8),
                ha='right', zorder=6)
t.set_path_effects(stroke)

t = ax.annotate(f'IRT rec. → G = {G_IRT:.2f}',
                xy=(N_IRT, G_IRT), xytext=(240, 0.33),
                fontsize=6.5, color='#777777',
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color='#aaaaaa', lw=0.7),
                zorder=6)
t.set_path_effects(stroke)

t = ax.text(460, 0.82, 'Reliability threshold (G = 0.80)',
            fontsize=6.5, color=GRAY, ha='center', va='bottom',
            bbox=dict(facecolor='white', edgecolor='none', alpha=0.8, pad=1))

ax.text(350, 0.06, 'Below reliability threshold',
        fontsize=6.5, color='#cccccc', ha='center', fontstyle='italic')

# --- Axes ---
ax.set_xlim(0, 700)
ax.set_ylim(0, 1.0)
ax.set_xlabel('Number of items')
ax.set_ylabel('Generalizability coefficient (G)')
ax.set_xticks([0, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700])
ax.set_yticks(np.arange(0, 1.1, 0.2))

ax.yaxis.grid(True, alpha=0.12, lw=0.4)

plt.tight_layout()

# --- Save ---
outdir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
for ext in ('pdf', 'png'):
    fig.savefig(os.path.join(outdir, f'fig3_dstudy_curves.{ext}'))
plt.close()

# Verification
print('Saved fig3_dstudy_curves.pdf + .png')
for label, ni, C in [('Multi@55', 55, C_MULTI), ('Multi@200', 200, C_MULTI),
                      ('Single@200', 200, C_SINGLE), ('Single@552', 552, C_SINGLE)]:
    print(f'  {label}: G = {ni/(ni+C):.3f}')
print(f'  IRT@116 (single): G = {G_IRT:.3f}')
print(f'  Ratio: {N_S80/N_M80:.1f}x')
